title: An Australian law firm says 87 percent of enabled staff use ChatGPT
friendlyTitle: An Australian law firm says most enabled staff now use ChatGPT
summary: On 12 November, OpenAI published an interview with Sam Nickless, chief executive of Gilbert + Tobin, an Australian corporate law firm. He says 87 percent of enabled ChatGPT users are active, more than twice the firm's usual rate for a new tool. He also says a confidential partner-review job, run in ChatGPT Work, cost about $62. The firm says people still define the task, check the output, and own the result.
friendlySummary: On 12 November, OpenAI published an interview with Sam Nickless, the chief executive of Gilbert + Tobin. He says 87 percent of staff who were given ChatGPT use it. That is more than twice the firm's usual rate for a new tool. He also says one confidential review job cost about $62. People still have to check the work and own the result.
whyItMatters: This is the firm's account, on OpenAI's site, not an independent audit. The useful part is the boundary he describes. A custom assistant can hold his writing and working style so a report can test a draft before the meeting. He says it does not decide, and it does not speak for him. If you run a professional firm, the check is the same: a secure tenant, no client data in the open tool, and a person on the final work.
